verdict.rationale: Testing in isolation from production is a fair question for a voice-agent framework with a hosted cloud, so the axis applies. The evidence shows no sandbox or test mode. The local development runner runs the agent on the developer's own machine and is explicitly described as not a sandbox. Pipecat Evals run against the real agent and its real services, so they give no isolation from production data. The OpenAPI spec's mention of running mocks is only a developer building block, not a product-provided sandbox, so it earns no credit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data
